Base directory for this skill: /Users/owner/.ovld/claude/marketplace/plugins/overlord/skills/overlord-mission

# Overlord Mission

Use this core whenever an agent connector needs to work with Overlord, whether the session was launched by Overlord Desktop/CLI or the user asks from chat to engage with Overlord. Treat **ticket** as a user-facing synonym for **mission**: invoke this `overlord-mission` skill for either term. There is no separate `overlord-ticket` skill.

Connector adapters may add harness-specific commands, hooks, MCP tools, or launch flags, but they must not replace the lifecycle rules in this core.

## Mode 1: Launched From Overlord Desktop Or CLI

Use this mode when the prompt already contains a mission ID or explicitly says the session was launched by Overlord.

**`<mission_id>` is always the short display id** — `coo:695`, `1:899`: a workspace prefix, a colon, and a number. Pass it as `--mission-id`. **`<objective_id>`** is the objective display id (`coo:695.k7xm`) or UUID; pass it as `--objective-id` when you know which objective to execute. Never pass an objective id as `--mission-id`. If the prompt includes `OVERLORD_OBJECTIVE_ID` or an Objective ID line, include `--objective-id` on attach. If the only id you can find is a bare UUID with no mission display id, re-read the prompt or run `ovld protocol search-missions` rather than guessing.

**An objective display id is a complete address.** `coo:695.k7xm` already spells its mission, so `--mission-id` is optional on every command whenever you pass a full objective display id as `--objective-id`; Overlord derives `coo:695` from it. This is the identifier to reach for when reconnecting to a mission that is running more than one objective, where "the active objective" is ambiguous and a mission id alone is not enough. An objective **UUID** names no mission, so it still needs `--mission-id` alongside it.

1. Attach first with `ovld protocol attach --mission-id <mission_id> [--objective-id <objective_id>]`.
2. The attach response prints JSON to stdout containing `session.sessionKey`. The CLI also persists this key automatically so subsequent `ovld protocol` commands in the same working directory resolve it without `--session-key`. If auto-resolution fails, pass `--session-key <sessionKey>` explicitly on every subsequent call.
3. Treat the Overlord mission prompt as authoritative for the objective, constraints, and delivery target. Begin executing the current objective immediately after attach; do not wait for more instructions or ask for confirmation. This differs from `connect` or `load-context`, which only retrieve mission context and never imply the agent should act.
4. Post updates while working: `ovld protocol update --session-key <sessionKey> --mission-id <mission_id> --summary "..." --phase execute`.
   During long mechanical stretches with nothing meaningful to post, send `ovld protocol heartbeat --session-key <sessionKey> --mission-id <mission_id> [--phase execute] [--note "..."]` instead of an empty update.
5. Follow-up messages after the initial mission are captured automatically by the installed `UserPromptSubmit` hook and stay in discussion intent while the mission is in review. Do not post `user_follow_up` manually unless the hook is unavailable.
6. If blocked, call `ovld protocol ask --session-key <sessionKey> --mission-id <mission_id> --question "..."` and stop.
7. Deliver last with `ovld protocol deliver --session-key <sessionKey> --mission-id <mission_id> --summary "..."`. Normal delivery is summary-only; objective-ledger evidence syncs independently.

When review facts genuinely apply, you may add `deliveryReport.agentReport` through `--payload-json` / `--payload-file`: use
`humanActions`, `tradeoffsMade`, `knownRisks`, `deferredWork`, and `assumptions`, with empty arrays
when none apply. Human actions are concrete work a user must perform outside completed agent work;

content.text:
Not expected, and you don't need to re-pair. Here is what happened.

**Cause.** Your Mac approved the phone correctly, but the helper Desktop launches for that link died immediately with `revoked controller`. The phone keeps its identity key across the app reinstall and across your four retries, so the Mac's device store now holds five records with that same key. The first one is the old ICE-era record I revoked during cutover, and the lookup took the first match instead of the active one. So the authority refused a controller you had just approved, Desktop kept restarting the helper (that is the relay admission every ~30 s in the control-plane log), and the phone saw its freshly authenticated link close before its first request.

**Fix.** A key now resolves to its active record, and to the newest revoked one only when none is active; a regression test re-enrolls a revoked key and checks both outcomes. The fix is in the `latch` binary only. A signed, notarized payload with it is building now (version bump, about four minutes); I'll install it, and the existing pairing (the last one, `e8ee3d03…`) should come up on its own since the phone retries with backoff. If the phone shows "Pairing required" instead, foreground the app once. I'll tell you when it's installed.

content.text:
Two real defects, both now fixed and covered by tests that fail on the old code:

1. **Authority lookup** picked the first record for the phone's key (a revoked one). Fixed in `latch`; you saw the helper come up after that, but the phone still failed because of the second defect.
2. **Enrollment receipt lost at close.** The Mac helper writes the encrypted receipt and closes the link in the same breath, and the link layer aborted its transport task before the last frames were sent; the phone side also dropped its connection the instant the carrier closed, even with the receipt still buffered. Both ends now drain within a bounded 3 seconds. This is the "final response before close" protection the plan required; the composed tests had not exercised a close immediately after the last write.

The second fix is in the shared native library, so it needs a new phone build and a new Mac payload. Both are building now (a few minutes), and I'll reinstall the phone app over USB and the Mac payload when they finish. After that, do one more pairing from scratch (revoke the current iPhone entry on the Mac first, then Pair a Device again); the phone should show the session list within a few seconds of your approval.

Same-LAN automated rows are done and both gates hold, but the LAN entry is not being used: the phone's Bonjour browse finds no Mac even with a 1.5 s window, while the Mac advertises the service on three interfaces. That needs two things only you can check on the iPhone. Here is the status and what I need.

**Measured, same LAN (phone on your Wi-Fi, VPN off), recorded as `docs/field-runs/same-lan-20260908T085431Z.json`**

| Row | Attempts | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold opens (real launches over USB) | 30 | 30/30, launch to usable gateway p50 923 ms, p95 1500 ms, max 1617 ms |
| Reconnect cycles, LAN allowed | 30 | 30/30, resume to usable gateway p95 1030 ms |
| Reconnect cycles, relay only | 30 | 30/30 |

All 90 went over the relay. Gates: cold open ≤ 5 s met, explicit recovery ≤ 5 s met.

**Fixed along the way** (committed as `6dc55a8`): a suspend/resume ordering race and a serialized snapshot loop that stalled the phone for 20 s after every resume; the Mac helper now audits its link lifecycle; the harness passes `--` before app arguments.

**Please check on the iPhone**
1. Settings → Apps → Latch → is **Local Network** switched on? If iOS never showed the prompt, toggle it on. Without it the app cannot browse for the Mac and will always use the relay.
2. Settings → Wi-Fi → tap the (i) next to your network: what is the phone's IP address? The Mac is 192.0.2.10; if the phone is on a different subnet or a guest network, LAN discovery cannot work there.

**Manual subset on this network, whenever you have two minutes** (the app is installed and paired; leave Auto-Lock at Never): open a session's terminal, type `pwd` and Enter, confirm the output; send one conversation message to any session and approve one action if one is pending; open a preview. Tell me what you saw and roughly how long each took. After that, turn Wi-Fi off and tell me; I'll run the cellular rows over USB.

Same subnet as the Mac (192.0.2.10 and 192.0.2.10), so discovery should work there. That leaves the Local Network permission as the likely blocker. Please check Settings → Apps → Latch and tell me whether **Local Network** is on; if it is off or missing, switch it on and I'll rerun five LAN-allowed cycles immediately.

Meanwhile I'll look at the browse from the Mac's side once more and keep the rest of the matrix ready.

content.text:
Here is where things stand.

**Done and measured (all commits pushed; evidence in `docs/field-runs/`)**
- Cutover complete: relay and control plane deployed on Railway (one replica each, sleeping off, migration 0007 applied), signed and notarized Mac payload and Desktop installed, phone paired, sessions preserved.
- Same LAN, both carriers, real attempts over USB: LAN path 30/30 cold opens p95 474 ms and 30/30 reconnect cycles p95 429 ms; relay path 30/30 cold opens p95 1500 ms and 60/60 cycles p95 1030 ms. Both gates hold.
- Relay restarts: 10/10, recovery p95 1.8 s. Lease renewal observed three times at the 5-minute marks. Helper restart via Desktop swap recovered in 2 s.

**Problems found and fixed today** (each with a regression test where the code allows): revoked-record lookup blocked pairing; enrollment receipt lost at link close on both ends; suspend/resume ordering race; snapshot loop serialized behind a hung request; Bonjour browser discarding the Mac (no TXT record); `.local` target outlasting the LAN bound; racing LAN and relay is unsound because Rust connects cannot be cancelled, so the phone now goes LAN then relay; Desktop's helper restart schedule never resetting after a healthy run; the Mac publishing unreachable bridge addresses.

**Running right now:** the gateway-restart row. Then I reinstall the helper and phone build with the last two fixes and rerun the helper and gateway rows (about 25 minutes). The phone went to background once during the helper row (one gap of four kills unobserved), so please leave it untouched until I say.

**Still to do, in order**
1. Control-plane outage row (automated, after the restart rows).
2. Manual subset on this Wi-Fi: you, ~2 minutes when I say "go".
3. Cellular rows: you turn Wi-Fi off; I run 30 cold opens and 30 cycles (~20 min).
4. 20 Wi-Fi/cellular switches (you toggle, I watch a terminal), 20 long-suspension foreground cycles (I can automate by bringing another app forward for minutes at a time), 10 Mac sleep/wake cycles (you wake the Mac), lease expiry (needs the Mac cut off from the control plane for 10 minutes; I'll need `sudo` for a firewall rule or you to unplug the Mac's network), UDP-blocked hotspot and NAT64 network (I set them up on the Mac, you join from the phone).
5. APNs: blocked on your Apple developer steps (Xcode sign-in, Push capability on the App ID, an APNs key).
6. 24-hour soak with resource baselines, then the final notarized coordinated release, retired TURN variable deletion, and the reports and runbooks updated with every number.

Continuing with the restart rows now.
